senses.gloss:
1náva, a. new; of an earthen dish, (fresh,
i. e.) unburned. [prob. fr. nú, ‘now,’ q. v.:
cf. νέος, Lat. novus, Ger. neu, Eng. new.]

2náva [483^4], num. nine. [cf. ἐννέα, Lat.
novem, Ger. neun, Eng. nine.]

nāvā́, f. ship. [transfer-form (1209, 399)
fr. nau, nāv.]

náva-nīta, n. fresh butter. [perhaps
‘fresh-brought,’ as we say ‘bring the butter,
 i. e. make it come,’ in churning.]

návedas, a. perhaps well-knowing, cognizant
of (gen.). [apparently fr. an affirmative
particle na-, and vedas: see 1296^3
end.]
